name: Skip-Bo

setup.text: Shuffle the 162-card deck. Each player draws a card and the highest deals (Skip-Bo cards do not count). The deal passes left each game. Remove any blank cards.
Deal each player a face-down stock pile.
Turn the top card of your stock pile face up, without looking at the rest.
The dealer puts the rest of the deck face down in the middle as the draw pile. Building piles and discard piles start empty and grow during play.
The player to the dealer's left goes first.

turn.summary: Draw up to five cards, play as many as you can onto the middle building piles, then end by discarding one card.
steps: Draw cards to bring your hand to 5 (on your very first turn, draw 5).

Play the top card of your stock pile, the top of any of your discard piles, or a card from your hand onto a building pile. Piles go up in order 1 to 12, and a Skip-Bo card can stand in for any number.
Start a building pile only with a 1 or a Skip-Bo. Up to four building piles can be open. When a pile reaches 12, take it away and start a fresh one.
If you play all five cards from your hand, draw five more and carry on.
End your turn by discarding one hand card onto one of your four discard piles. You can also end a turn this way when you cannot or do not want to play.

round_end: If the draw pile runs out, shuffle the completed building piles to make a new one.
end: A game ends as soon as one player plays the last card of their stock pile. That player wins the game.

scoring.text: Optional: the winner of each game scores 5 points for each card left in opponents' stock piles, plus 25 for winning.
The first player to reach 500 points wins the series.

missed.text: Use stock pile cards first: the winner is the one who empties the stock pile, not the hand.
You may only play the top card of a discard pile, though you can stack any cards on it in any order.
Skip-Bo cards are wild, can start a building pile, and may be played as any number.
A player who draws too many cards must shuffle the extra cards into their own stock pile.
If someone plays out of turn and it is spotted before their turn is over, play goes back at once; that player then skips the draw on their next turn. If nobody notices, the turn stands.
